# Descent that removes a genuinely large coordinate

Author-derived, with no priority or independent-audit claim. This strengthens the geometric statement in `DESCENT_GEOMETRY.md`. The uncontrolled stochastic process is not replaced by these chosen words.

For each coordinate i let D_i consist of states x admitting an enabled reaction word to y<=x with y_i<x_i. Translation of the entire actual word shows D_i is upward closed. Dickson's lemma supplies a finite minimal basis B_i. Choose one witnessed word for each basis element. Across all nonempty B_i there are finite constants L and J bounding word length and total-count prefix overshoot. Both depend only on the raw reaction list, rather than a communication class or a growing inventory.

For any actual communicating class C,

    sup {x_i : x in C \ D_i} < infinity.                         (1)

To prove (1), otherwise choose a sequence in C\D_i with strictly increasing i-th coordinate. Dickson's lemma gives a comparable pair x<=z in that sequence, with x_i<z_i. Communication gives a word z->x, which witnesses z in D_i, a contradiction. If C\D_i is empty the assertion is immediate. No limiting stationary law is involved.

Consequently, outside a classwise finite box, choose a largest coordinate x_i. It exceeds the bound in (1), so an acquired basis word takes

    x -> x-delta,       delta>=0, delta_i>=1,

with length<=L and prefix total count<=|x|_1+J. Repeating such choices reaches a classwise finite head in at most |x|_1 words. All word-boundary counts decrease coordinatewise.

For the factorial energy E(x)=sum_i log(x_i!), each word decreases E by at least

    log x_i >= log(|x|_1/d),

whereas its prefix energy overshoot is at most J log(|x|_1+J). The first assertion uses the decrement of the chosen largest coordinate; the second uses at most J net positive particles in a prefix and the bound log(m!)−log(n!)<= (m−n)log m. If J was originally only a total-count overshoot, replace it here by the maximum sum of POSITIVE coordinate increments over every chosen word prefix. This is still a finite raw-list constant and controls factorial energy even when particles are converted between species.

# Coordinatewise deletion words: a representation of the whole class

This is an author-derived use of monotone reachability and Dickson's lemma. Its historical novelty is not established. It is a geometric construction, not yet the physical-clock recurrence theorem.

For a finite raw reaction list define D to be the set of count states x from which an enabled finite word reaches y<=x, y!=x. The inequality is coordinatewise. D is upward closed: the same word translated by z>=0 takes x+z to y+z. Therefore D has a finite minimal basis B. For each b in B choose one actual deletion word w_b, ending at b-delta_b with delta_b>=0 nonzero. There are finitely many words, so their maximum length L and maximum prefix count overshoot J are finite and depend only on the raw list.

Let C be ANY actual communicating class. Then C\D is finite. Otherwise Dickson's lemma gives two distinct states x<=y in that infinite set. Communication supplies an enabled word y->x, so y is in D, a contradiction. This step uses actual communication, not an asserted stationary law.

Thus every state of C outside the finite set H_C=C\D dominates a basis vector b and has an acquired word

    x -> x-delta_b,

whose terminal counts ALL decrease or stay fixed. Iterating such words reduces the integer total count at least once per word and reaches H_C in at most |x|_1 words. The total length is at most L|x|_1. Every prefix stays below |x|_1+J because word-boundary counts decrease. This is a linear-length descent path with a constant count overshoot, not a serpentine path of length |x|^d.

For a weakly reversible network the word stays in the same closed communication class by translated complex return paths. The statement does not assume a conserved total or freeze any low coordinate. A finite conserved class simply lies entirely in its finite head if no deletion is possible. A conserved enzyme pool forces deletion words to return its actual phase, so several evolving inventories and bounded phase coordinates are retained in the representation.

This gives a genuine alternative to transporting one Green profile between neighboring inventories: the global geometry is encoded by finitely many monotone deletion templates and a classwise finite terminal set. # Exact finite cells, with their acquisition and limitation

Same author and scope as this stage. These facts are mathematical constructions, not a general recurrence theorem.

Use raw mass-action propensities q_e(x)=kappa_e x!/(x-y_e)!, interpreted as zero unless x>=y_e. For a linkage class C_l and an integer residual z>=0, form the COMPLETE translated cell

    S_(l,z)={z+y:y in C_l},

with all its complex-graph edges. The full generator is exactly the sum of these cell generators. A physical edge x->x+y'−y has the unique residual z=x−y for that raw reaction. Parallel edges remain separate or their rates are added.

## A reference acquired from the finite raw graph

For every raw edge choose a finite directed return path in its strongly connected linkage class. Add one unit of flow around that edge followed by its return path. Summing these cycles gives strictly positive integer coefficients kappa0_e, with equal total incoming and outgoing flow at EVERY complex. This is a constructive finite operation on the supplied graph.

Let mu0(x)=1/x!. On each reference cell,

    mu0(z+y) q0_e(z+y) = kappa0_e/z!.

Complex flow balance therefore proves stationarity of mu0 restricted to that cell. More generally EVERY FINITE UNION OF COMPLETE CELLS has exactly mu0 restricted to each communicating component as a stationary measure. Cell overlaps do not spoil the identity. Selecting arbitrary individual edges would spoil it. This is an exact acquisition, rather than a supplied stationary fiber or mixing assumption.

For the original rates let

    a=min_e kappa_e/kappa0_e,    b=max_e kappa_e/kappa0_e.

On a finite irreducible union with m distinct states, the directed matrix-tree formula compares each rooted tree weight by factors a^(m−1), b^(m−1). Hence its normalized original stationary law pi obeys

    (a/b)^(m−1) mu0(x)/mu0(y)
      <= pi(x)/pi(y)
      <= (b/a)^(m−1) mu0(x)/mu0(y).                 (1)

The same comparison holds with aggregate rates: every aggregate edge ratio remains in [a,b]. No spectral-gap lower bound is used.
